$schema_note: Acknowledged `supabase migration repair` placeholder rows, per target, for scripts/check-migration-safety.mjs. Read out of git's object store at HEAD, never from the working tree, so an untracked, symlinked, or hardlinked file at this path cannot substitute for the reviewed blob. A placeholder row is one with statements IS NULL: it asserts a version is applied without recording what content was applied, so history stops being proof of what is live. Listing a VERSION here means a human already reconciled that version against the live schema and accepts it as baseline noise. Per-target (not one flat list) also means an acknowledged TEST placeholder can never be reused to authorize a PRODUCTION push, and pins the expected project identity so the gate refuses if it is ever run against the wrong database for a given target. Adding entries must be a reviewed commit, never a runtime flag, so an automated loop cannot acknowledge the very row that should have stopped it.
$how_to_extend: If the gate refuses with an unknown-placeholder error, confirm the new placeholder version against the live schema first (e.g. compare live function/table definitions, not just history), then add the version string to the relevant target's placeholder_versions array and COMMIT. An uncommitted edit has no effect: the gate reads HEAD.
$identity_keys: project_ref is matched exactly against PGUSER (postgres.<ref>) or PGHOST (db.<ref>.supabase.co), never as a substring. database is compared to PGDATABASE and to the live current_database(). db_system_identifier would bind a target to one specific physical Postgres cluster via pg_control_system().system_identifier; it is left null (unpinned) for both real Sandra targets below because a live check during this baseline's creation found sandra-production and sandra-test reporting the IDENTICAL system_identifier -- evidence that Supabase provisions at least some managed projects from a shared template/snapshot rather than a fresh initdb per project, so this value does not reliably distinguish Sandra's own prod from its own test on Supabase's infrastructure. project_ref (exact, anchored) plus the live current_database() check are the enforced identity signals today. Every key must be present explicitly -- an absent key would be an accidental opt-out.
$out_of_order_esign_retimestamps: 20260901181004_record_definitive_esign_template_provider_create_failure.sql was retimestamped to 20260902120000 and 20260902074814_esign_atomic_disconnect_state.sql was retimestamped to 20260902120100 after later eSign versions reached shared backends first. These are not placeholder-baseline entries: a database that already applied the old versions will still see the renamed files as new pending versions because Supabase's ledger is keyed by version. Their SQL is idempotent, so applying the fresh versions is safe and leaves both old and new version rows as history.
